params.body:
## What

Generation and lifestage become two axes, as in the Gentells Standard and in Maarten's own filter: sector, then generation, then lifestage.

- **Generations** (`generation_tags`, when someone was born): Gen Z, ZAlpha, Gen Alpha.
- **Lifestages** (`lifestage_tags`, a new column, where someone is now): kids, tweens, teens, students, young adults, and young families. Young families is still proposed in the standard.

Until now one list held both. The classifier wrote Gen Z next to Teens as if they were the same kind of thing.

## The data moves with it

Migration `cohorts-split-2026-09-26` (`packages/core/cohort-split.mjs`, run from `db.mjs`, with trends run from `store.mjs` where their table is created). Simulated read-only on the production database before this pull request:

| Table | Tagged | Rewritten | Gets lifestages | Dropped tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| signals | 102,430 | 98,031 | 97,664 | 15 |
| articles | 35 | 16 | 16 | 0 |
| insights | 72 | 72 | 72 | 0 |
| gold_set | 22,879 | 21,588 | 21,206 | 14 |

- **Nothing is lost.** Every row it changes first leaves its old value in `cohort_split_undo`.
- **Old ids follow the standard.** `gen-tweens` becomes `ls-tweens` through the standard's `replacedBy`. Old Sanity references (`{_ref}`) in trends become plain ids.
- **Stray spellings are mapped only where they can mean one thing.** `gen-z`, `gen-teenagers`, `gen-teen` and `gen_students` are mapped. The rest (`gen-gamers`, `gen-millennials`, `gen-parents`, `gen-adults`, `gen-creators`, `gen-women`) is dropped and counted in the migration note.
- **It is fast.** Timed at 617 ms for 102,000 rows with the stamp triggers on. A second run changes nothing.
- **The migration log is left alone.** `classification_log` is history of what a model said at the time.

## Writers and readers

- **Prompts.** `getTaxonomy()` now serves generations and lifestages from the standard instead of the `generation_segments` table. The start-up sync could only ever add rows to that table, so shrinking the list in code would have kept all seven segments in every prompt. The sync no longer writes generations. The table stays for its Sanity-era birth years, which are a starting point for the birth-year question to Maarten.
- **A long-standing bug.** The classify prompt showed birth years as `[object Object]`. That is fixed.
- **Classify, process, consensus and the gold set, suggest, posts** (create, update, import) and the post keyword guesser all go through `splitCohorts`. Whatever shape a writer uses, each tag lands on its axis.
- **The observatory tools** (`cohorts`, `signals`) read the column of the axis asked about. Their descriptions name both lists, taken from the standard.
- **The Mix** gets a Lifestage axis, and Cohort is relabelled Generation. There are no stored wishes on it.
- **Endpoints.** `/internal/taxonomy` and `/taxonomy` carry `lifestages` and `lifestage_label`. Trend and post projections carry `lifestage_tags`, which the site already has columns for.
- **The ladder contract and the paper appendix** name `lifestage_tags` on signals and insights. The paper still verifies 201 of 201 claims.

## Tests

925 pass. The new `test/cohort-split.test.mjs` (11) covers:

- mapping old, stray and unknown tags;
- the migration on signals, trends with references, and the gold set;
- the undo rows, and that a second run is a no-op;
- the version stamp on rewritten rows;
- classify with the log, suggest, and posts on create and on an old-shape edit.

With the `replacedBy` rule broken, 8 of the 11 fail.

## After merge

The site follows in its own pull request: the lifestage vocabulary, a label for `ls-*` ids, and the filter. Until then the site shows the generation label where there is one and nothing for a trend that only had lifestages.
params.title: Generation and lifestage are two axes
